title: Scene
description: A staged unit of action: a fight, a conversation, a search of a room. It is preparation, not history — a scene that is played produces an event in the record, and the scene stays as the thing that was set up. The type says what kind it is, and a medium that stages other kinds adds its own codes rather than its own resource.

perspective.description: Out-of-universe by default: an encounter is preparation. Playing it produces an event, which is in-universe.

type.description: What sort of scene it is.

campaign.description: The campaign it is prepared for.

cell.description: Quadtree cell token of the battle map it is fought on.

difficulty.description: How hard it is meant to be. Games rate this; other media do not.

adversary.description: What the party faces, and how many of each. Games cast these as stat blocks; other media leave it unset.

played.description: The event it produced, once it has been played.
